lead: Vancouver plumbing deals with rain, older homes near downtown and cold snaps from the Columbia Gorge. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Vancouver.
risk: aging pipes in older homes, wet crawl spaces and frozen pipes in east wind cold snaps
risk_short: old pipes, wet crawl spaces and frozen pipes
why: Hough, Arnada and Uptown Village have homes from the 1900s to the 1940s with galvanized supply lines and clay sewer laterals. East Vancouver and Felida were built mostly after 1970.
Long rainy seasons strain crawl-space drainage and sump pumps. Cold east winds from the Columbia Gorge freeze exposed pipes a few times most winters.
water: Vancouver pumps all of its water from wells in deep aquifers under the city. It is moderately hard and needs little treatment.
tips: Check your sump pump before the rainy season.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
Disconnect hoses when an east wind is forecast.
areas: PipeMend works in Uptown Village, Hough, Arnada, Fourth Plain, Fisher's Landing, Cascade Park, Felida, Salmon Creek and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Vancouver Community Development Department, and plumbers must hold a certificate from the Washington State Department of Labor and Industries.

faq.q: Is this Vancouver, Washington or Vancouver, BC?
faq.a: This page covers Vancouver, Washington, across the river from Portland, Oregon. PipeMend serves U.S. cities only.
